source_caption:
The Little Prince is more than a simple adaptation of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry’s beloved novella. Directed by Mark Osborne, the film expands on the spirit of the original story while preserving its emotional core, blending stylized CGI with beautiful stop-motion animation inspired by Saint-Exupéry’s watercolor illustrations.

Rather than retelling the book scene for scene, the film frames the story through a young girl growing up in a world ruled by schedules, expectations, and routine. Her friendship with an aging aviator slowly opens the door to the Little Prince’s universe, where imagination, love, and human connection matter more than logic or achievement.

Like the original 1943 novella, the film quietly explores themes of loneliness, innocence, grief, and the way adulthood often strips people of wonder. Saint-Exupéry wrote The Little Prince during exile in World War II, and beneath its fairy-tale simplicity lies a deeply philosophical reflection on human nature and emotional truth.

What makes the 2015 adaptation stand out is how gently it translates those ideas for modern audiences. It doesn’t rely on spectacle as much as feeling, reminding viewers that the most meaningful things in life are often invisible, fragile, and impossible to measure.

source_details.synopsis: The Little Prince (French: Le Petit Prince; Italian: Il piccolo principe) is a 2015 English-language French-Italian animated fantasy adventure comedy-drama film directed by Mark Osborne and based on the 1943 novella of the same name by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. The film stars the voices of Jeff Bridges, Rachel McAdams, Paul Rudd, Bud Cort, Marion Cotillard, Benicio del Toro, James Franco, Ricky Gervais, Paul Giamatti, Riley Osborne, Albert Brooks and Mackenzie Foy. It is the first adaptation as a full-length animated feature of The Little Prince.
